learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how democracy reaches the grassroots level! Understand Panchayats, Municipalities, and the power of local self-governance.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Local governments solve local problems efficiently because local people understand their issues better than politicians sitting in Delhi or the state capital. It brings democracy to the doorstep.
These historic amendments gave constitutional status to local governments. The 73rd is for rural areas (Panchayati Raj), and the 74th is for urban areas (Municipalities).
It created a uniform three-tier system: Gram Panchayat (village level), Mandal/Block Panchayat (intermediate level), and Zila Panchayat (district level).
The amendments mandate that one-third of all seats and chairperson positions be reserved for women. Seats are also reserved for SCs and STs in proportion to their population.

State Election Commissions were created to conduct regular elections. State Finance Commissions were set up to ensure local bodies receive adequate funds to perform functions (like water supply, local roads) listed in the 11th and 12th Schedules.

fun_activity.title: 👥 Mock Gram Sabha
fun_activity.instructions: Gather your family or friends. Pretend you are the 'Gram Sabha' (all adult voters of a village). The issue: You have funds for either a new well or a new school roof. Debate and vote on how to spend the money locally!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly outline the major changes brought by the 73rd Amendment.
📌 Know the difference between Gram Panchayat (elected representatives) and Gram Sabha (all registered voters in the village).
📌 Be ready to discuss the challenges local governments still face (like states not transferring enough funds or real power).
quick_recap: ⭐ Local governance ensures decentralization of political power.
⭐ The reservation for women in local bodies was a revolutionary step for women's political empowerment.
⭐ Elections to local bodies must be held every five years.
